subject: exercise-sports-science
title: Energy Systems: Three Systems Sharing One Bout

slides.heading: Energy Systems: Three Systems Sharing One Bout
bullets: How ATP-PC starts with the largest share at 70 percent while the phosphocreatine store is full, anaerobic glycolysis peaks at 55 percent as lactate builds, and the aerobic system ramps up to 75 percent - with all three systems contributing throughout one continuous bout
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one continuous bout of exercise and watch three energy systems share the work, with only their shares changing.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Describe the handover in order: all three systems on together, ATP-PC fading as the phosphocreatine store drains, glycolysis peaking as lactate builds, the aerobic system ramping up to dominate
Explain why no energy system ever switches completely off during the bout
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to state the share of each system at any stage of the bout and explain why the shares change.

slides.heading: Starting a sprint - but what supplies the energy a minute later?
bullets: The phosphocreatine store is tiny and drains within seconds, yet the athlete keeps moving
If the first system fades, what takes over - and does anything ever switch off completely?
slides.notes: Ask the class: if ATP-PC fades after about ten seconds, why does the athlete not stop? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the other systems were already working from the first second.

slides.heading: All three systems overlap - only the shares change
bullets: All three systems are active from the first second and overlap throughout the bout; only the largest contributor changes
ATP-PC starts largest at 70 percent, glycolysis peaks at 55 percent around 30 seconds, and the aerobic system reaches 75 percent in longer work
At every stage the three shares add to 100 percent and none of them is zero
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: the handover is a shifting overlap of shares, never a clean switch from one system to the next.

slides.heading: All three systems switch on together
bullets: In the first seconds ATP-PC holds the largest share at 70 percent while the phosphocreatine store is full
Anaerobic glycolysis already supplies 20 percent and the aerobic system 10 percent - all three are on from the first second
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the three bars: every system is already contributing, with ATP-PC largest only because its store starts full.

slides.heading: The phosphocreatine store drains and ATP-PC fades
bullets: About 10 seconds in, the draining phosphocreatine store can no longer sustain ATP-PC, which fades to 35 percent
Glycolysis rises to 40 percent and the aerobic share climbs to 25 percent - nothing has switched on or off, the shares have moved
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and watch the store gauge drain: ATP-PC shrinks because its fuel runs low, while both other shares grow.

slides.heading: Glycolysis takes the largest share as lactate builds
bullets: About 30 seconds in, anaerobic glycolysis holds the largest share at 55 percent and lactate builds as it works
The aerobic share keeps climbing to 35 percent and ATP-PC still contributes 10 percent
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and compare the bars: glycolysis is now largest, but the aerobic bar has grown at every stage and ATP-PC has not vanished.

slides.heading: The aerobic system ramps up to dominate
bullets: Minutes in, the aerobic system supplies most of the energy at 75 percent as oxygen delivery rises
Glycolysis still supplies 20 percent and ATP-PC 5 percent - the other two still contribute, so there is no clean switch at any point
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and check every bar: aerobic dominates, yet no bar is at zero, which is the whole point of the handover.

slides.heading: Worked example: reading the shares at 30 seconds
bullets: At about 30 seconds the shares are ATP-PC 10 percent, glycolysis 55 percent and aerobic 35 percent, which sum to 100 percent
The aerobic share has climbed from 10 percent at the start to 35 percent, while ATP-PC has faded from 70 percent to 10 percent
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, read the three shares at 30 seconds. Step 2, check they sum to 100 percent. Step 3, name the largest contributor - glycolysis. Step 4, compare with the first seconds, where ATP-PC was largest at 70 percent.

slides.heading: Your turn: read the shares
bullets: In pairs: state the share of each system in the first seconds and minutes in, and name the largest contributor at each stage
Then swap and check: did your partner leave any system at zero, or claim one system switched off?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for overlap reasoning, then take two pairs answers: ATP-PC largest first, glycolysis largest at about 30 seconds, aerobic largest minutes in, with all three always contributing.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says the body uses only one energy system at a time
Name the shares at the first seconds, at about 30 seconds and minutes in to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers follow all three shares through the whole bout and show that none ever reaches zero.
